entries.unit: Load Balancing at the Frontend — public chapter
sections: Load Balancing at the Virtual IP Address

mechanism.owner_quote: Load balancing chooses among eligible backends. The invariant is that no request reaches an ineligible backend and no retry loop is unbounded; it needs fresh health/selection signals and retry-safe callers.
mechanism.reason: Explains selection signals as the basis for distributing requests and that they are not equivalent.

invariant.owner_quote: Cap request cost at the interface where one request can dominate a backend, and test the selector under the real cost distribution.
invariant.reason: SRE page has no per-request cost cap or selector test under real distribution.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A least-loaded or active-request selector assumes that a backend with spare capacity will do useful work. A seriously unhealthy backend can instead return an error in milliseconds, so its active-request count falls and the selector sends it more traffic. The backend becomes a sinkhole.
failure_recovery.reason: Describes fast-error attraction and the sinkhole failure it produces.

alternative.owner_quote: Compare round-robin, random choice, least-active requests and affinity against request cost, stale load signals and state placement.
alternative.reason: Names competing selection policies but gives no condition that reverses the choice.

sections: Note: summed container usage can hide one container high usage
Note: HPA supports metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1 not v1
Migrating Deployments and StatefulSets to horizontal autoscaling

mechanism.owner_quote: Horizontal scaling multiplies processing replicas; vertical scaling changes resources available to existing replicas.
mechanism.reason: States the scaling mechanism (adding replicas) directly.

invariant.owner_quote: Neither can increase throughput past a serial or externally fixed bottleneck.
invariant.reason: K8s HPA page has no serial-bottleneck throughput ceiling.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A new replica may start cold, contend on a shared dependency or amplify connection churn; test scale-out under a burst and bound the work each replica can claim.
failure_recovery.reason: Names scale-out failure modes and the required test/bound.

alternative.owner_quote: Vertical scaling or a queue/backpressure policy may be preferable when the bottleneck is per-replica resource or the workload cannot partition.
alternative.reason: Page does not compare vertical scaling or queue backpressure.

mechanism.owner_quote: vertical scaling changes resources available to existing replicas
mechanism.reason: States the vertical mechanism: enlarge the resources of existing replicas.

invariant.owner_quote: Neither horizontal nor vertical scaling can increase throughput past a serial or externally fixed bottleneck.
invariant.reason: States the capacity ceiling that vertical scaling cannot exceed.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A resize usually needs a restart or migration, so the old capacity is unavailable during the change; bound the maintenance window and keep a fallback.
failure_recovery.reason: Names resize unavailability and the required fallback.

alternative.owner_quote: Horizontal scaling or sharding may be preferable when the workload partitions and a single node is an unacceptable failure domain.
alternative.reason: K8s page does not compare horizontal scaling or sharding.

mechanism.owner_quote: Autoscaling is a **feedback-control mechanism**, not a promise of immediate extra capacity. A signal must be collected, interpreted, acted on, and followed by resource provisioning, application readiness and dependent-service capacity.
mechanism.reason: KEDA local text is only the landing page; no control-loop or capacity content.

invariant.owner_quote: A signal must be collected, interpreted, acted on, and followed by resource provisioning, application readiness and dependent-service capacity.
invariant.reason: KEDA local text is only the landing page; no control-loop or capacity content.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: During that delay, new demand still reaches the old infrastructure.
failure_recovery.reason: KEDA local text is only the landing page; no control-loop or capacity content.

alternative.owner_quote: Scheduled capacity or static headroom may be simpler when demand is predictable or the scale-out path is slower than the burst.
alternative.reason: KEDA local text is only the landing page; no control-loop or capacity content.

mechanism.owner_quote: A cell-based architecture runs multiple copies of the serving stack, each with a routing key and a data partition
mechanism.reason: Defines the cell as a bounded population with independent capacity and failure domain.

invariant.owner_quote: The boundary is only real if every dependency is cell-scoped.
invariant.reason: States that shared dependencies defeat a nominal cell boundary.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A shared database, queue, cache, control plane or configuration publisher can make all cells fail together
failure_recovery.reason: Names shared-control-plane blast radius and the required test.

alternative.owner_quote: A single deployment with failure-domain isolation may be preferable when the population is small and cell duplication cannot be justified.
alternative.reason: Names single deployment with failure-domain isolation.

sections: Limitation: decreasing the tenant shard size
Does shuffle sharding add additional overhead to the KV store?

mechanism.owner_quote: A shuffle shard selects a random subset of workers for each tenant
mechanism.reason: Explains the subset selection and partial tenant overlap.

invariant.owner_quote: Hash-based assignment alone does not prove statistical independence.
invariant.reason: Safety rule against assuming hash-based independence.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A failed worker affects every tenant whose subset includes it

alternative.owner_quote: A fixed cell anchors one tenant to a known home and population boundary.
alternative.reason: Contrasts fixed cells and the dedicated-home condition.

mechanism.owner_quote: A deployment stamp is an independently operated deployment unit used for scale, isolation or locality.
mechanism.reason: Defines the independent deployment unit and its purposes.

invariant.owner_quote: It needs a routing key, a state authority, a deployment and upgrade process and a rule for shared global dependencies.
invariant.reason: Lists the routing, authority, upgrade and shared-dependency preconditions.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is configuration drift or split state across stamps; version the stamp definition, route by an explicit key and reconcile state at the authority.
failure_recovery.reason: Names drift and split state, with versioning, routing and reconciliation controls.

alternative.owner_quote: A cell-based deployment is the alternative when isolation is the main goal and scale is secondary.
alternative.reason: Names a competing mechanism and the condition that reverses the choice.

mechanism.owner_quote: Geode places identical regional nodes behind a global routing layer so clients can use a nearby healthy region.

invariant.owner_quote: It needs a data replication and consistency contract, a regional health signal, a routing rule and an explicit failover authority.
invariant.reason: Lists the replication, health, routing and authority preconditions.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is a route to a stale or isolated region; the router must use an authoritative health and data-freshness signal, and failover must fence the old writer.
failure_recovery.reason: Names stale routing and prescribes health/freshness signalling plus fencing.

alternative.owner_quote: Active-passive recovery is the alternative when cross-region consistency is not worth the routing complexity.
alternative.reason: Names a competing mechanism and the condition that reverses the choice.

mechanism.owner_quote: Static content hosting publishes immutable objects to an object store or CDN origin and serves them by URL without per-request application compute.
mechanism.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

invariant.owner_quote: A retained version is the rollback path
invariant.reason: Requires cache key, freshness and authorization to agree for served static assets.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Cold-cache miss storms and incomplete purges are common; exercise origin failover and a known purge.
failure_recovery.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

alternative.owner_quote: A dynamic origin or edge compute may be preferable when content changes per request or publication cannot be governed.
alternative.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

entries.unit: Architectural Approaches for a Multitenant Solution — Microsoft Learn

mechanism.owner_quote: Tenant-based isolation assigns each tenant a bounded share of compute, storage and quota, with routing and credentials that keep the tenant scope explicit.
mechanism.reason: Defines per-tenant compute, storage and quota with explicit routing and credentials.

invariant.owner_quote: No query, cache key, queue consumer or credential may cross a tenant boundary without an explicit shared-resource contract.
invariant.reason: Forbids crossing tenant boundaries without a shared-resource contract.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A shared cache or background worker leaks one tenant's data or consumes another's capacity; scope keys by tenant and test indirect paths with a foreign identifier.
failure_recovery.reason: Names shared-cache and worker leaks and requires tenant-scoped keys and foreign-ID tests.

alternative.owner_quote: A shared pool with tenant-scoped predicates is cheaper at low scale; choose dedicated resources when noisy-neighbour or compliance risk dominates.
alternative.reason: Contrasts a shared pool with tenant predicates against dedicated resources.
